main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling sambal belacan given the others' complaints about smell in work calls, rooms and laundry; resolved with a compromise: cook after 7pm, window open, notify C beforehand.

A-B.evidence: A proposed the combined arrangement (T14) and B said 'Yes, that works for me' (T15); B's earlier stance was that timing didn't matter (T8).

A-C.evidence: C first said the time doesn't matter (T11), then agreed 'works for me' (T17) to A's summary of the plan (T14).

A-D.evidence: A first asked for no strong-smelling food and D resisted (T4). A then softened to cooking after 7pm (T5); D accepted the combined plan: 'That works for me too' (T19).

B-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (T2, T3) and later separately accepted the same arrangement (T15, T17); they never addressed each other directly.

B-D.evidence: D asked B what would work (T9); B said open the window and he'd shut his door (T10); D agreed to the plan including the open window (T19).

C-D.evidence: C said the window and timing don't help the laundry (T11); D offered to give advance notice (T12); C said 'that works' (T13) and D accepted the final plan (T19).
